firstrun.title: Welcome to ShellyLanMan
firstrun.text: ShellyLanMan discovers, monitors and manages Shelly devices on your local network. It is based on ShellyScanner by usnasoft.
firstrun.authNote: UI authentication is off by default. Only run ShellyLanMan on a network you trust, or put it behind a reverse proxy with authentication.

Ctrl+Space complete · Ctrl+/ comment the lines · Ctrl+Shift+U / Ctrl+Shift+L upper / lower case · Tab / Shift+Tab indent
The output pane shows the script's print() lines while it runs from this editor (the device's websocket debug log is switched on when needed).
Script editor settings are in Settings → Script editor.

sch.help:
Each line is a job: when it runs (time, or before/after sunrise or sunset, days, weekdays and months) and what it calls on the device.
The expression field can be edited directly (seconds minutes hours day month weekday).
● enables or disables a job on the device at once; the other changes are written with Apply.
Double-click a parameters field (or use the ▾ menu) to edit known parameters; ▶ runs the call now.
Load ... adds the jobs of a backup file; they are written with Apply.
action.chartsTip: Measures charts of the selected devices
chart.none.title: No devices chosen
chart.none.text: Select one or more devices on the Devices page and press Charts.
chart.help.title: Help
chart.help:
The readings of the last 24 hours are kept by ShellyLanMan, so a chart starts with history; new readings are added as the devices are refreshed.
Drag over the chart to zoom in; drag with the mouse held to move the time window. While paused the mouse wheel zooms. Resume (▶) returns to the live view.
Ctrl+R changes the range, Ctrl+P pauses or resumes, Ctrl+C copies the image.
The CSV layout (series one after the other, or side by side) and the default graph are in Settings → General.
help.title: Help
help.devices.title: Devices table
help.devices:
Click a row to select it; Ctrl+click and Shift+click select several. Double-click opens the device information (or its web page, see Settings → General).
Ctrl+F goes to the filter, Ctrl+E clears it, Ctrl+S changes the filter column. The toolbar actions work on the selected devices.
help.settings.title: Devices settings
help.settings: Settings opens FW Update, Wi-Fi 1/2, restricted login, MQTT and other settings for the selected devices; each apply reports one result line per device. Changes for off-line devices are queued (Deferred page).
help.checklist.title: Checklist
help.checklist: A row per device with the settings worth checking (eco mode, LED, logs, Bluetooth, access point, roaming, Wi-Fi, range extender, scripts, automatic firmware update). Right-click a cell for the actions of that column.
help.firmware.title: Firmware and local download
help.firmware: The devices check for new firmware themselves; tick stable or beta and press Update. The Shelly index column compares each device with Shelly's firmware index; ⚡ shows a QR code to download that firmware from ShellyLanMan with a phone, for updating a device through its own access point.
help.backup.title: Backup and restore
help.backup: Backups are kept by ShellyLanMan (Settings → Network, backups per device) and can be downloaded. Restore asks the same questions as ShellyScanner (other device, passwords, scripts) and needs a confirmation.
help.scheduler.title: Scheduler
help.scheduler: Jobs of Gen2+ devices, thermostat profiles of the Wall Display and rules of the BLU TRV. The ? button in the scheduler explains the editor.
help.scripts.title: Scripts and KVS
help.scripts: Scripts of Gen2+ devices: run, stop, enable, upload from a file or a backup, download and edit (the ? button in the editor lists the shortcuts). The KVS tab edits the key-value store.
help.charts.title: Charts
help.charts: Select devices and press Charts. ShellyLanMan keeps 24 hours of readings; see Help under the chart for zoom, pause and export.
update.help: Off by default. When on, the server asks GitHub once a day for the releases of ShellyLanMan; nothing else is sent.
about.what1: ShellyLanMan is a network-based tool for monitoring and managing Shelly IoT devices. It automatically discovers devices on the local network and shows key information such as Wi-Fi strength, cloud connectivity, uptime, temperature and meter readings. Devices can be controlled directly, and configuration backup and restore are available from the toolbar.
about.what2: Firmware management is built in, with a QR code for a quick download of the firmware, so you can update a device through the Shelly's own access point.
about.what3: An MCP server lets AI assistants such as Claude Code read and manage your devices, and as a Home Assistant app ShellyLanMan sits in Home Assistant's sidebar and adds its checks to your Shelly devices there.
about.dataValue: JSON files in the data volume, no database
about.free: ShellyLanMan is free and open source, and always will be. If it saves you time, a coffee (or a few tokens for coding) is welcome — and never expected.
about.basedOnSS: The functional and code reference: every feature, the terminology and the Shelly know-how come from ShellyScanner by {author}.
about.basedOnMD: {author} gave the idea, the inspiration and the basis of the look and feel with MikroDash.
about.basedOnSM: {author}'s Shelly-MCP was the model for ShellyLanMan's MCP server: its tools for AI assistants, the confirmation gates and scenes.
about.coffeeFor: Beyond the credits, {author} deserves a coffee too.
server.invalid: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
server.confirm: ShellyLanMan will move to port {port} now; this page then opens on the new port. Bookmarks, a reverse proxy or a Docker port mapping (bridge mode) must be changed as well.
server.proxy: ShellyLanMan now listens on port {port}. Change your reverse proxy to that port.
server.help: With host networking the port is opened directly on the host. In bridge mode keep the port and change the mapping (-p) instead.
server.fixed: Set by SHELLYLANMAN_LISTEN: change it there.
mcp.intro: ShellyLanMan can serve AI assistants (Claude, local models) through the Model Context Protocol at /mcp: they can list and read your devices and, if you allow it, switch them. Everything stays on your LAN: devices are reached directly, never through the Shelly cloud.
mcp.access.control: Read and control (switches, lights, covers, thermostats, scenes, backup, reboot, firmware)
mcp.access.configure: Read, control and configure (also scripts, KVS, schedules, webhooks, virtual components, scenes, RPC calls, device login)
mcp.accessHelp: Reboot, firmware updates, deletes, script code, RPC writes and device login also need the assistant to confirm explicitly. Every action is written to the log.
mcp.tokenSet: A token is set. It is shown only once; make a new one if you lost it (the old one then stops working).
mcp.tokenShown: Copy the token now: it is not shown again.
mcp.tokenConfirm: Make a new token? Assistants that use the current one lose access.
mcp.warn: The token gives access to your devices: keep it secret. Do not expose ShellyLanMan to the internet.
